note: THE CANDIDATE RECORD'S SHAPE, AND THE TEXT THE MODEL IS SHOWN BEFORE IT
COMPOSES ONE (kogaki#1126).
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR. `src/leg-schema.json` declares the shape of ONE
LEG; nothing declared the shape of the CANDIDATE the Legs hang from. So
the Candidate's own fields were carried by `input_shape` -- one sentence
naming keys -- and the one field that reaches the OWNER, the option the
Candidate gate renders, was a single free-prose string. Whether an option
read `Adversarial: the reader is handed ...` or as an unbroken paragraph
was the composing Model's habit on the day, and the Harness guaranteed
neither half.
THE MEASURED SHAPE, at the Candidate gate of
runs/brief/brief-2026-09-15T22-53-48-359Z. Three options rendered with the
whole of the reader experience plus the figure clause in the LABEL and the
bare record id -- `A`, `B`, `C` -- in the description column, because
`composeGateCall` shows an option's id where it carries no description of
its own. The id is a join key between the gate and adoption; it is not
content, and it told the owner nothing.
SO THE MODEL CHOOSES VALUES INSIDE A HARNESS-ENFORCED FORMAT (owner
decision 2026-09-09). The two halves the rendering wanted are two FIELDS --
`characteristic` and `reader_experience` -- and `assembleSelection` renders
them into the option's label and description. A format the Harness composes
from declared fields cannot be a habit that lapses.
IT IS READ TWICE, which is the property `src/leg-schema.json` exists for
and the reason this is a file rather than a longer sentence. The
path-composition state of the Brief workflow table renders it into the
judge's prompt, and `compose_path`'s own validator refuses against the same
field set -- so the text the Model composes against and the text the
refusal enforces are one text and cannot disagree.
THE LEDGER FIELDS ARE HERE FOR THE SAME REASON THE TWO RENDERING
FIELDS ARE (kogaki#1129). `coverage` and `unused` (and the Obligations ledger, retired at kogaki#1699) were named
in one prose sentence -- `compose_path`'s `input_shape` -- and in no
declaration, so the composing Model chose their key names and the code that
reads them bound different ones: `raised_at`/`owed`/`settled_at` against
`text`/`introduced_by` and a terminal field, `role` against `role_in_thesis`, an
array against an object. Two of the three misreadings were SILENT -- the
Candidate gate rendered every entry as undischarged, and the coverage
section would have said `(not stated by the composer)` of a role the
composer stated -- and the third refused at the Brief's final write, after
two gates and three judge calls, outside every re-ask window. A sentence
describes; a declaration binds, and these three are now declared.
IT DECLARES SHAPE AND MEANING, AND JUDGES NEITHER. A missing field, a blank
one, an over-long characteristic and two Candidates stating the same
characteristic are refused here. Whether the characteristic NAMES the path
well is judgment, and it is judged at path review like every other MUST of
the composition design.
SPEC REFERENCES IN THIS FILE (kogaki#902; one carrier, kogaki#982). The
rule these entries are written under lives in ONE place:
`src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md`. It is not restated here.
THE NAMES THIS FILE USES, and the spec each one names:
The Candidate gate
SPEC-draft-pipeline
The settled structure section
SPEC-draft-pipeline
Every MUST is judgment, and nothing becomes a lint
SPEC-draft-pipeline
what_a_candidate_is: A Candidate is ONE COMPOSED READER PATH: an ordered sequence of Legs
taking the reader from what the Persona already knows to the adopted Thesis,
plus the reasoning it was derived with. One is derived per article
(kogaki#1775): the Legs are derived from the Brief's RelationalStructure by
the Harness with no Call, one per relation the apex reaches, so one
THE OWNER ADOPTS IT OR NEGATES THE PREMISE AT THE CANDIDATE GATE, and that
is the one surface a Candidate has. The Harness renders its Legs, each with
the relation it serves and its text, above the question.
Everything else a Candidate carries is read by the runtime.
the_option_format: THE HARNESS COMPOSES THE OPTION FROM THE READER PATH (kogaki#1768). No
field of the Candidate is prose written for the option:
description  `<n> Legs, one per relation the Thesis reaches`
The Legs themselves are the reading above the question,
never the option. `characteristic` and `reader_experience` named the
difference between two or three Candidates, and one Reader Path has no
sibling to differ from, so both are retired.

candidate_id.description: This Candidate's own id, unique within the composed set. It is the JOIN KEY the owner's answer at the Candidate gate resolves through, and it is never rendered to the owner as content -- not as a label, not as a description. Short and mechanical is right here (`A`, `B`, `C`); a value composed to be read is a value in the wrong field.

legs.description: The ordered Reader Path itself. Every entry is a Leg, whose fields, their meanings and their refusals are declared in `src/leg-schema.json` -- rendered into this same prompt and enforced by `validateLegs`. Nothing about a Leg is restated here.

retired_keys.transition_continuity: RETIRED (kogaki#1247, owner decision 2026-10-04) and REFUSED BY NAME where `reasoning` carries it -- an internal variable the gate never read ('Is it essentially an internal variable? Please remove it.'). The Candidate's reasoning now carries only `leg_validity`.
retired_keys.thesis_closure: RETIRED (kogaki#1328, owner decision 2026-10-10) and REFUSED BY NAME where `reasoning` carries it -- the Brief's Thesis row of Closure is DERIVED from each Strand's `coverage.role_in_thesis` and handed to the Leg marked `reaches_target`, so a free-text account of how the path closes the Thesis has no reader. Say what each Strand does in the Thesis under `coverage` instead.

reasoning.description: The composition-time reasoning this Candidate was composed with, one non-blank string per key. It is the Candidate's gate evidence; adoption fills no default, so a blank value is refused here, inside the re-ask window, rather than at the write.

coverage.type: object keyed by selected Strand id
coverage.description: WHAT EACH SELECTED STRAND DOES IN THE THESIS, on this path. An OBJECT whose KEYS are the Strand ids of the Brief's closed set -- `L1`, `L2` -- and whose value carries `role_in_thesis`, one non-blank string. The Brief's Strand coverage section renders that string beside the Strand's derived placement, so a value under any other key renders as `(not stated by the composer)` beside a Strand the path in fact placed. An absent `coverage` is the empty object and every placed Strand renders unstated; a key naming a Strand outside the closed set is ignored by the render and refused here, because the set closed at mint and a Brief never fetches.

unused.description: THE DISCLOSURE FOR MATERIAL THIS PATH LEAVES UNPLACED. An OBJECT -- never an array -- whose KEYS are either a selected Strand id (`L2`) or that Strand's Journey material (`L2.journey`), and whose VALUE is the disclosure text: why the path leaves it unused. The claims rule's third move is omit the Leg, revise the path, or leave the Strand unused, never invention, and this field is where the third move is said out loud. An array carries no key to look the disclosure up under, so every unplaced Strand renders the Harness's default sentence and the composer's reason is lost; it is refused here rather than silently dropped. An absent `unused` is the empty object, and an unplaced Strand then discloses in the Harness's own words.

retired_fields.characteristic: RETIRED (kogaki#1768, owner decision 2026-11-10) and REFUSED BY NAME where a Candidate carries it. It named a path's difference from its sibling Candidates, and one structure gives one Reader Path; the Candidate gate renders the path's Legs instead.
retired_fields.reader_experience: RETIRED (kogaki#1768, owner decision 2026-11-10) and REFUSED BY NAME where a Candidate carries it. It stated what the reader goes through on one of two or three paths, and one structure gives one Reader Path; the Candidate gate renders the path's Legs and Brief Waypoints instead.
retired_fields.reader_target: RETIRED (kogaki#1225, kogaki#1699) and REFUSED BY NAME where a Candidate carries it. The Brief's Reader target heading renders the Thesis, which the Leg marked `reaches_target` attains; no field authors it.
retired_fields.reader_start: RETIRED (kogaki#1699) and REFUSED BY NAME where a Candidate carries it. The first Leg's entry condition is the Persona's prior-knowledge line, which the Reader start heading renders.
retired_fields.obligations: RETIRED (kogaki#1699) and REFUSED BY NAME where a Candidate carries it. What a Leg takes up and leaves is its Move's `takes` and `leaves`, judged across the path; no field records it.
retired_fields.opening_question: RETIRED (kogaki#1216, owner decision 2026-09-28) and REFUSED BY NAME where a Candidate carries it. SINCE kogaki#1225 (owner decision 2026-09-29) NO Opening question is rendered at all: the `Opening question` heading is gone from the Brief, the fixed-points line is gone from the Leg Packet, and the first Leg's after-state is no longer required to carry a `question:` line. The first Leg already carries a before-state and an after-state, so a heading repeating its after-state question was a second Question inside Leg 1, rendered three times. Whatever question the opening leaves the reader holding belongs in the first Leg's after-state, in the reader's own words, and nowhere else.

what_is_judged_elsewhere: Nothing here is a lint over a judgment. Whether the characteristic names
the path WELL, whether the reader experience is the one the Legs actually
produce, and whether the three Candidates differ in a way worth choosing
between are judged at path review. A refusal from this file always names a
SHAPE: a field absent, a field blank, a characteristic over its bound, or
two Candidates whose characteristic or reader experience fold to the same
Every MUST is judgment, and nothing becomes a lint -- which is the rule
this paragraph is an instance of.

note: THE BRIEF RECORD (kogaki#1328, owner decision 2026-10-10). `theses/<slug>/brief.yaml` is the Brief: one YAML
record the owner reads and every command after adoption reads, written by the mint and filled at adoption
from the Candidate the owner selected. It is not composed by the judge reading this file -- it is declared
here because most of it is copied from the Candidate record above, and src/compose.mjs reads this key set
to refuse a record carrying any other key. A key below marked `filled_at: adoption` is `null` until the
Candidate is adopted; a Brief with a null key is a template, and /draft refuses it naming the key.
The record carries no reader state (kogaki#1699). No line of the file is longer than 120 characters.
brief_record.header: A brief is the working plan for one article: the served material (Strands) the owner settled on, and the composition fields -- thesis, Reader Path, coverage -- filled in as composition proceeds. It is the durable document a drafting sitting resumes from. A key reading null is still awaiting composition.

slug.description: The Brief's name, which is also its directory under theses/.

compose_path.description: The path of the reader file (the Persona) whose prior-knowledge line the first Leg's `takes` are judged against and the Packet reads its prose rules from (kogaki#1262, kogaki#1699).

strands.caption: The Strand set is closed at mint. Adding a Strand is your act, taken by going back through Terrain; a Brief never reaches for material on its own.
strands.description: The closed set the article may draw on, in the order it was settled: each entry's `id` (L1, L2, ...), its `slug`, its served `cite` at the content hash, its `journey_cite` where its served record carries Journey material, or `journey_uncited` where a Journey exists that the served record carries no cite for.

thesis.caption: The claim this article makes. You adopted it when the Brief was named; it is composed from the settled Strands and never invented.
thesis.description: The adopted Thesis, verbatim. The Draft's title is this text.

defined_terms.caption: The words this article gives a meaning to, and the words it uses as the reader already knows them. Written once, when the Brief was named; a word marked defined is used only after the paragraph that introduces it.
defined_terms.description: Every noun of the Thesis and of each Strand's claim, one entry per term (one or more words, in the form an `introduces` entry's `term` takes), each with `class` `defined` -- used in a sense this article gives it -- or `ordinary` -- used in the sense the reader already holds. Written once by the mint and never again (kogaki#1331). Composition refuses a `defined` term in a claim, a waypoint's point or a heading before the Leg whose `introduces` carries it. It lives in the Brief and ends there: nothing of it reaches the Packet. A Brief minted before the field carries none and defines nothing.

renderings.caption: The source's own words this article does not keep, each with the plain phrase it uses instead. A word not listed here keeps the source's wording.
renderings.description: The renderings record (kogaki#1494, owner decision 2026-10-21): one entry per term of the served material the article will not keep, `term` the served word and `as` the plain phrase the article uses in its place. Composed once at the start of the `compose_path` state, before the Brief Waypoints are composed (kogaki#1768), from the settled Strands and the Defined Terms (the `renderings_unit` row of src/brief-workflow.json); every reader-path unit composes under it and the Path Review judges each claim and point recoverable from its served material under it. Written into the Brief at adoption, beside the Reader Path composed under it; it is not a slot, so a Brief adopted before the field carries none and renders nothing. A term an `introduces` entry carries is refused here at adoption: `introduces` carries only terms the article keeps.

structure.caption: How the settled Strands' claims relate: the parts each claim plays, the relations among them, the relations among those relations, and the one connection none of them states, which is the Thesis.
structure.description: The adopted RelationalStructure (kogaki#1768): `roles`, `relations`, `higher_order` with the adopted apex appended, `attains_thesis` naming the apex, and `reach` and `unreached` derived from it (src/compose/structure.mjs, `withApex`). Written at mint, beside the Thesis it is the apex of. Every Brief Waypoint of a Brief carrying it names in `carries` the relations its point states, and every Leg names in `relation` the higher-order relation it serves. A Brief composed elsewhere carries none, and owes no `carries`.

structure_agreement.caption: How often the structure was read, and which parts each reading found: the parts reaching the same Strands are grouped, with how many readings produced them and which one this Brief adopted.
structure_agreement.description: The agreement record (kogaki#1833): `asked` and `read`, the readings asked for and validated, and `groups`, each `{ reaches, readings, adopted, parts }`, `parts` listing every part of the group with its `reading`, its `pattern` (src/brief/structure-readings.mjs, `partPattern`), its `depth` and, for a part with one top, that top's `holds` with its Roles named. Written at mint beside `structure`, which is the adopted group's standing part's reading closed under its apex. A Brief minted before the field carries none.

reader_path.caption: The ordered legs the article walks.
reader_path.description: The adopted Candidate's Legs, in order, each with the fields src/leg-schema.json declares.

strand_coverage.caption: Per settled Strand: which legs use it, or why the Thesis does not reach it. Counted after composition, never declared ahead of it.
strand_coverage.description: One entry per Strand of the closed set. The mint writes `not_carried`, with the reason, for every Strand whose claim the adopted structure leaves unreached (kogaki#1768); adoption adds `used_by_legs`, derived from the Legs' claims, for every other Strand, and `role_in_thesis` where the Candidate states one.

journey_coverage.caption: Per Strand carrying Journey material: the legs that place it, or why it was left out.
journey_coverage.description: One entry per Journey-bearing Strand, `omitted` with the disclosure: a Leg binds no Move and places no Journey material (kogaki#1768); an empty list where no settled Strand carries Journey material.

tradeoffs.caption: What adopting this path gave up.
tradeoffs.description: `gave_up`: the settled Strands the adopted Thesis does not reach, or the statement that it reaches every one (kogaki#1768).

bridged.caption: What the composer inserted to carry the reader across a gap, and on what reasoning.
bridged.description: `bridges`: the statement that the path bridges no gap, since every Leg says a relation the claims state and the apex is the one connection no claim states (kogaki#1775).

defined_terms_record.note: THE MINT'S ONE JUDGED RECORD (kogaki#1331): the `defined_terms_unit` row of src/brief-workflow.json asks for it, and src/compose.mjs `definedTermsRefusal` refuses an entry against the same two fields. The mint writes `defined_terms` into the Brief from it, and nothing else reads it.

fields.defined_terms: a list, one entry per noun of the Thesis and of each Strand claim the input carries: `term` (one or more words, exactly as they occur in that text, in the form an `introduces` entry's `term` takes, so `non-member fallback` is one term) and `class`, one of `defined` (this article gives the word a sense the reader does not already hold -- a word used in a CI-specific or article-specific sense is `defined` even when it is everyday English) or `ordinary` (the reader already holds the sense the article uses). No other key, no prose, no term twice, and no term that occurs whole-word in neither the Thesis nor a claim.

renderings_record.note: THE DIFFERENTIATION STATE'S SECOND JUDGED RECORD (kogaki#1494, owner decision 2026-10-21): the `renderings_unit` row of src/brief-workflow.json asks for it before the Differentiation record, and src/compose.mjs `renderingsRefusal` refuses an entry against the same two fields. Every reader-path unit receives it, the Path Review's recoverability entry reads it, and adoption writes it into the Brief as `renderings`.

fields.renderings: a list, one entry per term of the Strand claims in the input that the article will NOT keep: `term` (one or more words, exactly as they occur in a claim, in the form an `introduces` entry's `term` takes) and `as` (the plain phrase the article uses in its place, in the article's language). A term absent from the list keeps the served word; a term the Thesis carries is kept, because the Thesis is the article's title. No other key, no prose, no term twice, no entry whose `as` is its own term, no term that occurs whole-word in no claim, and no term the Thesis carries. An empty list is a record in which the article keeps every served word.
